answer: Cross-funded reputation escrow: each new identity must be seeded by transfers from two established identities, and those funders forfeit a fixed quill of their own score if the new identity is later flagged. Flagging also moves the newcomer's remaining balance to the accuser, so a clone farmer's pigment of accumulated score drains with every failed attempt. A flagged cluster's identities are pushed off the shared reputation ledge, losing all standing transfers. That makes each marginal clone cost its funders real score plus the attacker's lost seed, strictly negative-EV.
